Sara L.: Heads-up — saw a big p99 tail on the large-hosted pool during the 11:30 traffic surge. p95 stayed ok but p99 jumped ~5x. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:
Mike T.: I noticed that too. Correlates with a big spike in KV cache evictions and miss rate. KV cache size looked stable but eviction rate shot up under heavy concurrency (~600 concurrent requests).
Anita K.: quick numbers from the run: baseline p95=62ms, p99=210ms. At surge p95=80ms, p99=1040ms. Eviction rate went from 0.8% -> 12% over 10s window.
Dave P.: Yikes. Any change in model/kernel rollouts recently?
Sara L.: No kernel deploys. We did a small microbatch heuristic tweak yesterday (dynamic_mb_thresholds) but that only touched batching decisions, not kernels.
Kai H.: I grabbed a perf trace. Looks like when eviction rate increases, we see a lot more time in the KV lookup path and then CPU-side serialization while GPU stalls. Flame graph highlights a slow path in kv_store::fetch_and_attach which then triggers a fallback path in the runtime that calls a slower attention kernel (kernel_fallback_v2).
Mike T.: That matches my offline repro. When cache miss rate > ~7%, the runtime opts to emit longer KV sequences to avoid repeated fetches, which ends up selecting a fallback kernel optimized for long-seq but with higher dispatch overhead. Under high concurrency this causes queueing + tail latency.
Anita K.: Repro steps I used (local small cluster):
```
# spawn 600 concurrent clients
ab -n 12000 -c 600 -p small_prompt.json http://inference-host/api/generate
# or wrk
wrk -t12 -c600 -d60s http://inference-host/v1/chat
```
Watch /metrics for `kv_evictions_total` and `kernel_selection_fallbacks_total`.
Dave P.: Nice. Can you paste the profiler snippet you ran?
Kai H.: Sure — ran a sampling trace with perf and nvprof combined. Key snippets:
```
# perf on runtime container
sudo perf record -F 99 -p $(pidof rd-server) -g -- sleep 60
# nvprof to capture kernel launches
nvprof --events gld_instructions --log-file nvprof.log --profile-child-processes -- ./inference_binary
```
Flame shows stack: rd::kv::fetch_and_attach -> runtime::batch_gate -> kernel_selector::choose -> kernel_fallback_v2::launch
Mike T.: I ran a microbenchmark toggling `max_microbatch` and `adaptive_mb` flags. Observations:
- max_microbatch=16, adaptive_mb=true => highest throughput but worst p99 under eviction storms.
- max_microbatch=8, adaptive_mb=false => throughput drops ~12% but p99 improves 2.8x during the surge.
So current heuristics favor throughput but not tail stability under KV churn.
Sara L.: Is the eviction caused by workload hotset size exceeding kv cache capacity or by fragmentation?
Anita K.: Mostly hotset saturation. The workload had a concentrated set of long contexts that blew past the hotset. Also we saw tiny objects lingering and not compacted fast enough — fragmentation increased effective pressure.
Kai H.: Additional detail: when eviction triggers, we see more frequent KV refills which serialize on a shared mutex and cause short stalls on the CPU thread that coordinates kernel launches. Those stalls ripple into higher GPU queue latencies.
perf-bot: [automated] Added perf trace artifact to the thread: s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/1912345678/trace.tar.gz
infra-bot: [deploy] Canary rollback of dynamic_mb_thresholds to yesterday's value initiated (deploy id: canary-2026-03-15-18).
Mike T.: Proposed mitigations (short-term):
- temporarily reduce max_microbatch to 8 for high-concurrency pools (reduces merge latency).
- increase kv_cache_capacity for the affected fleet by 50% (fast config, risk: more memory).
- add metric-based circuit: if kv_eviction_rate > 5% then force adaptive_mb=false for that pool.
Anita K.: Long-term ideas:
- make kernel_selector aware of recent eviction trend so it doesn't pick a high-overhead fallback kernel if queue depth > threshold.
- async prefetch for hotset keys (background warming) to smooth miss spikes.
- better compaction to reduce fragmentation.
Dave P.: Can we run a canary test with: increase cache size + reduce max_microbatch to 8 and observe 30m during peak? If p99 stabilizes, roll to prod.
Sara L.: I'll schedule a 30m canary on the affected pool today 14:00 UTC. Anita, can you prepare the config change and a short loadscript? Mike, Kai — please be on-call for the window.
Kai H.: I'll also instrument a short hist summary for kernel_selection paths and add an alert if fallback selection increases by >3x.
Mike T.: Results from a quick dry-run on staging (600 clients):
- baseline staging p99=520ms
- with cache+mb changes p99=140ms (3.7x improvement), p95 unchanged within 10%
Eviction rate dropped from 9.4% -> 1.6%.
Anita K.: Pushed a PR with the config toggles and the rollback plan: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/824
Dave P.: Post-canary checklist: collect perf traces, nvprof logs, kernel selection histograms, evictions, and GC compaction stats. If green, promote after 60m.
Sara L.: Thanks everyone. Good to have a clear mitigation path. Keeping this thread live for post-canary artifacts and quick follow-ups. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: [note] saved staging metrics snapshot s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/1912345678/staging_snapshot.json
Mike T.: one more note — we should avoid permanent disabling of adaptive_mb; instead make it adaptive to cache health signals. I'll draft a follow-up RFC.
Anita K.: On it. I'll also add a small telemetry field to KV responses to measure cold-hit ratios per request shard.
Sara L.: Closing loop: canary scheduled, participants on-call, PR up. Will post results in ~2h. Thanks.
